logs.summary: Four leading medical societies have released unified vaccine recommendations for flu, RSV, and COVID-19, offering standardized guidance for healthcare professionals. Traws Pharma reported final Phase 2a results for its once-daily antiviral ratutrelvir, which showed fewer adverse events and no viral rebound compared to Paxlovid. A separate analysis found that COVID-19 vaccines delivered up to $809 in economic value per dollar spent in 2021, particularly benefiting high-income countries.

news.body: With ambiguity surrounding the federal vaccine recommendations, four leading medical societies have stepped forward with guidance for flu, RSV and COVID-19 vaccination. A panel led by a University of Maryland School of Medicine expert helped develop this unified approach, providing health care professionals with evidence-based guidance to help patients make informed decisions about protecting themselves against respiratory illnesses.

Colorado Springs Utilities drew down its water storage to the lowest level since 2014 to cope with persistent drought.

logs.summary:
A severe drought is affecting multiple regions globally as of late July 2026. In Europe, an "exceptionally serious" drought has hit half of England and all of Wales, while the Rhine River dropped to its lowest ever level in the Netherlands and the Danube reached record lows in Budapest, disrupting tourism and industry. In the United States, drought conditions worsened in states like Minnesota and Michigan, while other areas like the Grand Strand in South Carolina are lifting drought management plans, and parts of Virginia and North Carolina are seeing improvements.
New drought developments include worsening conditions in Maine and Minnesota, with 35% of Minnesota in severe drought, while South Carolina's Lowcountry remains under extreme drought despite summer storms. In Europe, record-low river levels continue to disrupt power output and transport, and wildfire risk is elevated across the continent. Jamaica faces a potential $500 million drought response, and drone footage highlights the drought's impact in England.

news.headline: Record-low Danube River affects tourism and industry as drought and heat grip Central Europe
news.body: As wildfires and successive heatwaves in France and Spain highlight climate change's impact, a severe drought is causing record low water levels on the Danube River, affecting tourism and industry. The river, which flows through 10 countries, has receded to unprecedented lows, exposing rocks and old shipwrecks. In Budapest, the Danube was measured at just 23 centimeters, breaking previous records. River cruise ships are docking upriver, and sightseeing cruises have been canceled. The drought has also affected Hungary and Romania's nuclear power plant operations, exposed a World War II bomb, and ended the summer season for excursion boat operators in Serbia.

incidents.summary:
Israel killed a senior Hamas commander described as involved in planning the October 7 attacks, an operation reported as coming two months after his predecessor was killed, with coverage characterizing the ceasefire as stagnating. Separately, Iran's High Council for Human Rights condemned what it called international silence and inaction over Israeli crimes in Gaza and urged concrete action to end impunity. The remaining item is an Italian artist's installation on the war's toll on mothers rather than a new conflict development.
A nine-month-old baby died of hypothermia inside his family's displacement tent in Gaza as winter returned, while Canada joined three allies in demanding Israel allow 150,000 tents into the territory amid winter storms battering makeshift camps. Gaza's Civil Defense recovered 70 bodies from destroyed homes in Beit Lahia and Jabalia after 231 hours of excavation, with more than 8,000 people still missing beneath the rubble. Separately, international media representatives voiced alarm over Israel's arrest of a video journalist, and an Israeli court upheld the detention of Palestinian land activist Ghassan Najjar until at least February 26.

On September 3, 2026, two Palestinian teens were killed in the occupied West Bank as Israeli settlers and snipers surrounded a village. Israeli forces bulldozed olive trees in the West Bank, while Prime Minister Netanyahu signaled plans to expand Israeli control over Gaza and the defence minister stated Israel still wants to remove Palestinians from Gaza. Additionally, a Gaza doctor continues to suffer torture in Israeli prison, and broader regional tensions escalated with Iranian missile and drone attacks targeting Kuwait.
On September 4, 2026, the UN raised 'ethnic cleansing' concerns over Israel's West Bank operation, reporting over 33,000 Palestinian refugees still displaced. Israeli police killed a Palestinian in Jerusalem after an alleged knife attack. Meanwhile, far-right minister Ben-Gvir outlined a plan for the forced expulsion of all Palestinians from Gaza.

logs.summary:
Israel killed a senior Hamas commander described as involved in planning the October 7 attacks, an operation reported as coming two months after his predecessor was killed, with coverage characterizing the ceasefire as stagnating. Separately, Iran's High Council for Human Rights condemned what it called international silence and inaction over Israeli crimes in Gaza and urged concrete action to end impunity. The remaining item is an Italian artist's installation on the war's toll on mothers rather than a new conflict development.
A nine-month-old baby died of hypothermia inside his family's displacement tent in Gaza as winter returned, while Canada joined three allies in demanding Israel allow 150,000 tents into the territory amid winter storms battering makeshift camps. Gaza's Civil Defense recovered 70 bodies from destroyed homes in Beit Lahia and Jabalia after 231 hours of excavation, with more than 8,000 people still missing beneath the rubble. Separately, international media representatives voiced alarm over Israel's arrest of a video journalist, and an Israeli court upheld the detention of Palestinian land activist Ghassan Najjar until at least February 26.

logs.summary:
Highway 160 over Wolf Creek Pass could partially reopen this weekend as southwest Colorado digs out from devastating floods. Record rainfall from the same system has provided rare relief to Southwest reservoirs, raising Lake Powell by 20 feet. In Palm Bay, Florida, flood-impacted women are delivering supplies door-to-door to other victims.
Flash flooding and flood warnings affected areas of Texas, Delaware, Portugal, and British Columbia, where a shelter-in-place advisory was issued. In Malaysia, flash floods killed two people while evacuee numbers dropped slightly, and recovery continued in Brevard County, Florida, with cleanup kits and debris collection. NASA imagery showed Navajo Lake surging from recent historic floods in the Southwest, and Nepal urged for improved early warning systems after its own devastating flood.

logs.summary:
A canal breach in Shropshire, UK, flooded homes, while a flooded street stranded cars in Wilmington, California. In Colorado, Wolf Creek Pass reopened after flood damage, and in Georgia, the flood emergency was extended as McCaysville lifted curfew and reopened a road to Tennessee. Elsewhere, Kenyans brace for heavy El Niño rains as flood survivors recall losses, Gaza’s humanitarian crisis worsens with heavy rain flooding tents, and Florida communities continue to struggle with flood recovery.
Florida floods prompted a chimp sanctuary to use drones for food deliveries, while a Lewis County family displaced by July floods received a new home. Kenya also faces economic strain from El Niño‑driven flood risks, with maize shortages and rising inflation.

logs.summary: A powerful magnitude 7.6–7.7 earthquake struck southern Panama on October 9, 2026, with its epicenter near Pitaloza Arriba in Herrera province. The quake triggered tsunami warnings for multiple countries across Central and South America, prompted evacuations and building shakes in Panama City, and caused some damage, though the Panama Canal was not affected. Initial USGS estimates of 8.0 were downgraded, and aftershocks were reported.

Iran hit back at President Trump's assertion that Tehran has been waging war since 1979, insisting the US cannot evade responsibility for aggression. Fresh missile threats against Saudi Arabia led major airlines to extend flight cancellations through 2027, worsening travel disruptions. Concurrently, Southeast Asian leaders opened their annual summit in Manila, prioritizing the ongoing conflicts' toll on energy costs and regional security.
Iranian strikes on US bases in Bahrain and Houthi advances forcing a Yemeni government retreat from Bab al-Mandeb have escalated Gulf tensions. In Gaza, Israel killed a top Hamas commander, while hundreds of oil spills from boat strikes pose a generational threat to Persian Gulf wildlife. Protests at the ASEAN summit clashed with police, reflecting regional opposition to the conflict and President Trump's visit.

news.body: Guatemala City, November 11 (QNA) â€“ The United States Geological Survey (USGS) reported that a 5.6-magnitude earthquake struck off the coast of Guatemala, causing buildings in the capital to shake. There have been no immediate reports of injuries or damage resulting from the earthquake. The USGS stated that the earthquake occurred 43 kilometers south of the coastal town of Puerto San Jose, at a depth of 35 kilometers. The tremor was also felt by residents in El Salvador and Nicaragua; both countries indicated that there is no risk of a tsunami. On September 16, a 5.3-magnitude earthquake struck southern Guatemala. Guatemala is located over an active geological zone, which frequently triggers strong earthquakes across Central American and the Caribbean. (QNA)
